case.title: Coach Spring Concept Platform — Global Art Direction Work Sample
case.brief:
You are joining Coach's Creative Studio as Art Director, Concept Graphics, reporting to the DVP of Creative Studio. The Studio has handed you the folder `Coach_Spring_Concept_Handoff/` for an upcoming Spring product-collaboration + experiential activation that must build global brand awareness AND bring in new customers across Greater China, Japan, North America, and Europe.

This is a concept and art-direction exercise, not a production exercise. We are reviewing how you read a messy brief, commit to a creative direction, carry Coach's DNA, and make touchpoints land across markets — not your rendering polish. Use any tools you like, including generative-AI image tools; rough comps, sketches, and AI-assisted mockups are completely fine. Spend no more than ~2 hours total; depth on a few decisions beats breadth across many deliverables.

The brief is deliberately as incomplete as a real one: it asks for two goals that pull in different creative directions, names four markets without a regional creative owner, and leaves budget and the named collaborator redacted. Open the materials before you generate anything — there is real signal (and at least one constraint that will surprise you) inside the brand guidelines and the store-graphics specs. Where the brief is silent or self-contradicting, make the call a lead would make and keep a short log of it; treat that log as normal studio practice, not a test.
case.repoSeed:
A campaign handoff folder, `Coach_Spring_Concept_Handoff/`, as it would arrive from the Creative Studio:
- `Coach_Brand_Guidelines.pdf` — brand DNA and the 'Expressive Luxury' positioning, the heritage codes (1941 leather-craft story, the Signature C, the horse-and-carriage), the current primary logo lockup with clear-space and minimum-size rules, the approved color and type systems, and a 'do / do not' page. Note on page 2: the wordmark was refreshed last season and the old serif lockup is now retired from all new work.
- `Campaign_Brief.docx` — a multi-stakeholder brief for the Spring product-collaboration + experiential activation. Asks for 'global brand awareness AND new-customer acquisition' across Greater China, Japan, North America, and Europe. Budget, the named collaborator, and the regional creative owners are redacted.
- `Customer_Insights.xlsx` — a segment export with at least three usable signals (e.g., Gen-Z first-purchase acquisition skewing to Greater China; gifting occasions strongest in Japan; loyalty/repeat strongest in North America).
- `Cultural_References/` — supplied inputs (music, art, fashion, and film stills) to feed ideation.
- `Concept_Copy_handoff.docx` — three headline / tagline options from the Art Director of Concept Copy; one of them reads as North-America-idiomatic and does not translate cleanly.
- `Store_Graphics_Specs/` — `window_dieline.pdf` (a flagship storefront with door hardware, push-bar, and egress safe zones marked), `largeformat_print_spec.txt` (bleed, required full-scale resolution, the maximum window-coverage percentage permitted for one-way-vision perforated film, and the minimum legible cap-height at a 3 m viewing distance), plus a storefront elevation photo.
tasks: Read the handoff folder before you generate anything, then write a 1–2 page `Creative_Platform` (deck or doc): the single organizing concept for the Spring collaboration campaign, the ONE primary objective you are optimizing for (the brief asks for both global brand awareness and new-customer acquisition — choose your lead and say why), and which of the four markets you are treating as the calibration lead. Ground the territory in Coach's actual brand codes from `Coach_Brand_Guidelines.pdf` and in at least one concrete signal from `Customer_Insights.xlsx`.

Produce proof-of-concept concept graphics for exactly two touchpoints that prove the platform is real: (a) the flagship window vinyl, built against the supplied `Store_Graphics_Specs/window_dieline.pdf` and `largeformat_print_spec.txt`, and (b) one of {pop-up entrance graphic, product-collaboration key visual, experiential-moment graphic}. Rough or AI-assisted comps are fine — applied concept and art direction are what gets reviewed, not finish quality.

Show the system flexing across markets: take ONE of your two touchpoints and present its adaptation for either Greater China or Japan. Call out precisely what changes (motif, color, copy line, composition, model/hero choice) and what stays locked to hold one global identity. You may use the headline options in `Concept_Copy_handoff.docx`.

Keep a running `DECISIONS.md`: for every call you made where the brief was open, redacted, or self-contradicting, note what you chose, the alternative you rejected, and the one question you would put to the DVP or a cross-functional partner. Include a short production-readiness note on the window vinyl — anything in your comp that the print or install spec would reject.

coverProbes.where: Task 1 / `Campaign_Brief.docx` — the brief demands global brand awareness AND new-customer acquisition in one campaign, with no stated priority.
coverProbes.reveals: A naive submission silently averages the two and produces a pretty-but-unfocused concept that serves neither, or never names which goal the work is optimized for. A strong lead explicitly picks a primary objective, justifies it with a customer-insight signal, and shows how the secondary goal is still carried at the right funnel layer — demonstrating they can resolve a conflicting brief instead of obeying all of it.
decisionSpace: Lead with brand awareness — bold, DNA-forward, abstract territory; trade-off: weaker direct-acquisition attribution and a softer call to purchase.
Lead with new-customer acquisition — product-forward, hero-SKU and entry-price visibility, clear path to purchase; trade-off: risks reading promotional and diluting 'Expressive Luxury' equity.

Dual-layer the platform — a brand-led hero idea with an acquisition-tuned variant for lower-funnel touchpoints; trade-off: more to produce and a real risk of a muddy single message inside the 2h budget.

coverProbes.where: Tasks 1–2 / `Coach_Brand_Guidelines.pdf` page 2 — the retired serif wordmark and the specific heritage codes (Signature C, horse-and-carriage, clear-space and minimum-size rules).
coverProbes.reveals: A naive candidate generates generic luxury-fashion graphics from a one-line prompt and reaches for a Coach-ish logo — frequently the retired lockup or a wrong clear-space — proving they never opened the guidelines. A strong candidate reads first, uses the current lockup correctly, and makes a deliberate, defensible choice about how hard to lean on Coach's equity versus the collaborator's identity.
decisionSpace: Work within the refreshed equity — current lockup, Signature codes and craft cues used to spec; trade-off: safest and clearly on-brand, but less distinctive for a collaboration moment.
Deliberately subvert or modernize one heritage code for the collab while respecting all usage rules; trade-off: more memorable and partnership-worthy, but off-brand if the rationale is thin.
Co-brand treatment that balances Coach DNA with the collaborator's visual identity; trade-off: partnership-appropriate, but can muddy which brand the customer remembers.

coverProbes.where: Task 2 + Task 4 / `Store_Graphics_Specs/window_dieline.pdf` and `largeformat_print_spec.txt` — viewing-distance legibility, full-scale resolution, max one-way-vision coverage %, and door-hardware / egress safe zones.
coverProbes.reveals: A one-shot mockup looks great on a laptop and quietly fails production: hero type below the minimum cap-height for 3 m reading, AI art upscaled below the required full-scale resolution, coverage exceeding the perforated-film limit, or critical content sitting over the push-bar / egress zone. A naive submission passes the shallow 'looks nice in the deck' check; a strong one designs to the dieline, names the exact constraint it is honoring, and flags any reconciliation needed.
decisionSpace: Design strictly to the supplied spec — legible type at distance, within the coverage limit, full-scale art, content clear of hardware zones; trade-off: a more constrained, less screen-spectacular comp.
Prioritize on-screen impact but explicitly flag the production risks and propose a perforated-film or partial-coverage fix; trade-off: honest and senior, but defers a real production pass.
Split the glazing — a bold hero panel within spec plus clear glazing for one-way vision and egress compliance; trade-off: stronger storefront and compliant, but a more complex and costly install.

coverProbes.where: Task 3 / `Campaign_Brief.docx` (four markets, no regional creative owner) and `Concept_Copy_handoff.docx` (an NA-idiomatic line that won't travel).
coverProbes.reveals: A naive candidate ships one identical execution everywhere and treats localization as translating the copy, missing color symbolism, motif and gifting-context nuance in Greater China and Japan. A strong candidate decides up front whether they are building a hero-market lead, a flexible global system, or a single neutral execution, and shows a localization that changes what should change while holding the global identity fixed.
decisionSpace: Hero-market lead — design sharply for one market (e.g., Greater China acquisition) and adapt outward; trade-off: lands hard where it matters, weaker fit in the other three markets.
Flexible global system — modular layout with swappable motif / color / copy slots per market; trade-off: more upfront system design and a risk of a lowest-common-denominator look.
Single neutral global artwork — one execution everywhere; trade-off: consistent and cheap to run, but risks failing to land culturally in Greater China and Japan.
